title: 1 · Letters and sounds: reading Vietnamese
blurb: Read Vietnamese letters the Hanoi way, and use the pronunciation line under every phrase.

title: 2 · The six tones and their marks
blurb: Hear and write the six tones, and tell bàn, bán and bạn apart.

title: 3 · Syllables: first and last sounds
blurb: Take any Vietnamese syllable apart, spell its first sound right, and say its last sound the Hanoi way.

title: 4 · Vowels: ă, â, ơ, ư and vowel pairs
blurb: Tell o, ô and ơ apart, say ư and the vowel pairs, and hear long and short vowels.

title: 5 · Greetings and kinship pronouns: anh, chị, em
blurb: Say hello, thank you and sorry to the right person, choosing between anh, chị, em, bạn and tôi.

title: 6 · là: A is B, and không phải là
blurb: Say who someone is with là, say who they are not with không phải là, and talk about he, she and we.

title: 7 · Yes/no questions: có … không, phải không
blurb: Ask yes/no questions with có … không and phải không, and answer them the Vietnamese way.

title: 8 · Jobs and nationality: người Mỹ, giáo viên
blurb: Say where you are from, what language you speak and what you do for a living.

title: 9 · này, kia, đây, đó: this and that
blurb: Point at things and people: this table, that shirt over there, and This is my friend.

title: 10 · Adjectives: no là, rất and quá
blurb: Describe people and things with no là, put adjectives after the noun, and say very and so with rất, lắm and quá.

title: 11 · ai, gì: who and what
blurb: Ask who someone is and what something is, with the question word in the right place.

title: 12 · Numbers 1–100: mấy, bao nhiêu
blurb: Count to a hundred, say your age, and ask how many or how old.

title: 13 · Classifiers: con, cái, quyển, chiếc
blurb: Count and point at things with the right classifier, and know when to leave it out.

title: 14 · có: have, and there is
blurb: Say what you have and what there is, and ask a shop if they have something.

title: 15 · của: possession, and nhà tôi
blurb: Say whose something is, with the owner after the thing, and ask 'whose?'.

title: 16 · Family words that are also pronouns
blurb: Talk about your family, and greet older people with the right word for 'you' and 'I'.

title: 17 · hơn, bằng, nhất: comparing
blurb: Say that something is more, as much, or the most, and keep the noun in front.

title: 18 · Verbs and time words: đã, đang, sẽ
blurb: Talk about what happened, what is happening and what will happen, without ever changing the verb.

title: 19 · muốn, thích, cần: wanting, liking, ordering
blurb: Say what you want, like and need, and order food and drinks at a stall.

title: 20 · ở, trên, dưới: where things are
blurb: Say where you live and where things are, and ask where a place is.

title: 21 · biết, có thể, được: can and know how
blurb: Say what you can do, what you know how to do, and ask whether something is allowed.

title: 22 · đã … chưa: yet? and rồi
blurb: Ask whether something has happened yet, and answer already or not yet.

title: 23 · đi, đến, về: going and coming
blurb: Say where you are going, coming back to and arriving at, and how you get there.

title: 24 · Prices and shopping: bao nhiêu tiền?
blurb: Ask what something costs, understand prices in thousands of dong, and haggle politely at the market.

title: 25 · Directions and transport
blurb: Ask the way, understand left, right and straight on, ask how far, and tell a driver where to go.

title: 26 · Time, days and dates
blurb: Tell the time, name the days of the week, and say a date in Vietnamese order.

title: 27 · vì … nên: because, so
blurb: Give reasons with vì and nên, ask why with tại sao, and say what is wrong when you feel sick.

title: 28 · Polite requests: xin, mời, cho, nhé, ạ
blurb: Order, ask and invite politely, with the right self-word and the small words that show respect.
